findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

On arrival a pan of water was observed stored in the hand washing sink in the kitchen, preventing easy access/use. This was pointed out to the PIC and the pan removed to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained easily usable at all time in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani bucket in the kitchen is observed at approximately 10 ppm CL. The PIC indicated that it was likely from last night and had not been changed today. This is not a sufficient concentration to effectively sanitize foods contact surfaces. Education was conducted and the bucket remade to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times in the facility. Change them as needed.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11(D) Reheating for Hot Holding. (D) Reheating for hot holding as specified under (A) - (C) of this section shall be done rapidly and the time the food is between 5C (41F) and the temperatures specified under (A) - (C) of this section may not exceed 2 hours. 

The gyro meat on the spit is observed with internal temperatures ranging from 28F-47F during this inspection. Per the PIC the spit was pulled from the freezer approximately two hours ago and not heated up immediately. Items on the spit should be cooked through completely in one process and the extra cooled and stored accordingly. The item was cooked during this inspection to correct the immediate violation.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. 

Cooked rice in portioned containers are observed in the reach in cooler across from the gyro spit. They are without date marking or tracking of any kind and were prepared yesterday (per the PIC). Education was conducted and multiple option (tracking the batches via white board, tracking dates on the individual containers, tracking batches with cycling the product, ect) given and the inspector will check what the decision for a process is at the scheduled follow up. Ensure that all TCS foods in the facility are marked for seven day date marking at all times.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

The hand sink in the kitchen area does not have functioning cold water. The only option is hot water at this sink and the water reaches scalding within 10-15 seconds. This does not promote adequate or safe hand washing practices. Per department head CK this could be a closing violation and needs to be remedied immediately. A follow up is being scheduled for 24 hours to ensure that a repair is completed. If it is not completed at that time the PIC is aware that closure will follow.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-305.11 Designation. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions. 

An employee phone was observed on that table in front of the three part sink where food preparation takes place. Education took place and the phone removed to correct the immediate violation. The table was re-sanitized as well. Ensure that employee belongings are stored so that they are not a concern for contamination of food contact surfaces or foods.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and that the PIC is instructed to ensure that employees are correctly educated in relation to hand washing procedures. Ensure that a clean barrier is used to maintain the freshly washed hands in a clean state.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to pass on this relevant information to employees and ensure that hand washing is taking place WHEN required at all times in the facility. Ensure hand washing happens at all times required.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Multiple cans of foods are observed with significant dents. Education was conducted with the PIC and the noted cans separated out for discard/credit. Ensure that all food packaging is in good condition until use. This is not a repeat at this time, but this situation has been noted earlier this year. Ensure that education is passed on to employees and procedures are consistently in alignment with food safety standards.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

Raw shrimp is observed over Ready-To-Eat (RTE) beef in the front standing cooler. This situation was discussed with the PIC and the items re-arranged during this inspection to correct. Education conducted. Ensure that safe storage order and separation of raw/Ready-To-Eat items in the coolers is taking place to prevent possible cross contamination. Store raw meats under RTE foods as well as according to their cooking temperatures.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

On arrival the cloth used for wiping counters in the front of the facility is observed being left on the counter between uses. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to store the cloth between uses in a sanitizer of sufficient concentration to maintain food safety standards. The rag was moved to the bucket to correct. It was also suggested to maintain an extra bucket in the front preparation area to allow for a more convenient safe storage location.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There is a buildup of grease on the floor behind the cookline where the fryers and flat top grills are being stored. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that floors, walls, and ceilings are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent grease buildup.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and the PIC instructed to ensure proper hand washing is taking place at all times moving forward. A clean barrier should be used after hand washing to prevent recontamination of the hands prior to food service.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

Raw chicken and beef are observed over opened containers of mayo, ketchup and mustard in the bottom section of the prep cooler. This situation was discussed with the PIC and the items re-arranged during this inspection to correct. Education conducted. Ensure that safe storage order and separation of raw/Ready-To-Eat items in the coolers is taking place to prevent possible cross contamination.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. 

A package of hot dogs is observed in the standing cooler next to the prep-cooler in the kitchen open and without a date marking. The PIC stated that the package was opened yesterday. Education was conducted and a date marking added to the package during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all Ready-To-Eat (RTE) foods in the facility are date marked after opening of their packages or preparation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING x2) 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

Ceiling tiles above the bathroom, sink, mop sink and prep areas are of the acoustic type and are not acceptable for food preparation or moist locations. The PIC was consulted and will be replacing as able moving forward.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs).

Allergen awareness training certification is not available for the only CFPM available at the facility. Education was conducted and a pair of hand outs attached to the emailed report. Ensure that the CFPMs at this facility have also completed allergen awareness training and the certificates are available moving forward.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager.

A the time of this inspection there is not a Certified Food Protection Manager available at the facility. The PIC was consulted and stated that the one they have on staff starts next week. A copy of the known local courses is being attached to this report and the PIC is instructed to insure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts at the facility.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW.

During this inspection the PIC could not produce verification that employees were notified of their responsibility to report illnesses and symptoms related to foodborne illness. A copy of the Reporting Agreement given out by this facility was found in the paperwork given during the pre-opening. Another copy is being attached to the email of this report. The PIC is instructed to have all food employees sign a a copy and maintain the copies at this facility moving forward.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Multiple cans of foods are observed with significant dents. Education was conducted with the PIC and the noted cans separated out for discard/credit. Ensure that all food packaging is in good condition until use.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

Raw chicken is observed over raw vegetables in the three door cooler in the prep room. This situation was discussed with the PIC and the items re-aranged during this inspection to correct. A hand out is being attached to the emailed report for an added visual.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

A bus tub of onions is observed on a shelf under cleaners, degreasers and bleach. Storage was discussed with the PIC and the container moved to correct. Ensure that all chemicals are stored in a manner that does not pose a risk of contamination for foods.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12(E) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(E) In a clean, protected location.

Two knives are observed being stored in the gap between two coolers. This gap is not able to be cleaned/sanitized. Education was provided and a new storage practice will be needed for these items. The items were moved to dish to correct the immediate violation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

A CL (bleach) based sanitizer is used in the facility. Only test strips effective for use with Quat sanitizers are available for checking the concentration of sanitizer solutions. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that the test strips and sanitizers match prior to the follow up.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING) 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

Ceiling tiles above the bathroom, sink, mop sink and prep areas are of the acoustic type and are not acceptable for food preparation or moist locations. The PIC was consulted and will be replacing as able moving forward.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING) 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

The triple sink has a small gap between it and the wall that could allow for moisture and mold growth. The PIC was consulted and instructed to seal (caulking suggested) prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

A the time of this inspection food handler training certificates are not available for the food handlers in the facility. Training was discussed and the PIC is instructed to have the training completed by the staff and the certificates available prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs).

Allergen awareness training certification is not available for the only CFPM available at the facility. Education was conducted and a pair of hand outs attached to the emailed report. Ensure that the CFPMs at this facility have also completed allergen awareness training and the certificates are available moving forward.
